commit.message:
Add promise settlement streaming helpers to code mode (#51126)

## What changed

Expose two JavaScript globals for consuming results as inputs settle:

- `as_settled(promises)` returns an async iterator of fulfilled and rejected records in settlement order, preserving queued results while the consumer is busy.
- `stream_settled(promises, emit)` delivers those records to a callback, awaiting each invocation and propagating callback errors.

Records include an `index`, a `status`, and either a `value` or a `reason`. Iterable inputs use positional indices; `Map` inputs retain their keys. Both helpers accept promises, thenables, and plain values.

## Testing

Add runtime coverage for ordering, input types, object identity, callback behavior, early iteration exit, and termination. Add stdio and gRPC host tests for partial results across waits, plus a scenario snapshot verifying fulfilled and rejected records reach the model.

GitOrigin-RevId: cddc9f3679ae04f2421e154caa0417afb15f550d

Clarify incremental tool namespace updates in Responses Lite (#51119)

## Why

Incremental namespace declarations contain only changed or added tools. Their descriptions need to make clear that previously declared tools remain available unless explicitly marked unavailable, and that redefinitions replace earlier definitions.

## What changed

Append this guidance to updates of existing namespaces, preserving any namespace description. Leave initial declarations and catalog hashes unchanged.

## Testing

Extend unit and request-history coverage for the namespace hint, unchanged turns that append no tool definitions, and MCP tool removals that append a standalone notice without rewriting history or repeating the notice on the next turn.

GitOrigin-RevId: e32f3c9948efb44a1253868fe67967f117cc21e8

Install full context in compaction replacement history (#51117)

## Why

Manual, pre-turn, and post-turn compaction previously deferred rebuilding initial context until the next turn. Their saved replacement history could omit refreshed instructions and skill catalogs.

## What changed

- Install initial context during local and remote compaction, before the last real user message or summary, keeping the compaction summary last.
- Persist matching full world-state and turn-context baselines with every replacement instead of retaining only partial extension metadata.
- Build replacement context and recompute token usage for the current model even when the previous model performs compaction. Reuse that captured context for eligible current-model retries.
- Capture manual compaction context centrally and propagate preparation errors to the task runner.

## Testing

Update assertions and snapshots for context ordering, refreshed instructions, resume and fork history, current-model checkpoint baselines, and cloud skill catalog retention across compaction and resume.

GitOrigin-RevId: 8572a76c31c6884a3c580b3bbb350d49af876bd1

Preserve trusted-tool context in Guardian Decisions requests (#51070)

## Why

The Decisions adapter rejected developer messages, including host-annotated trusted-tool context. Requests containing that context could not be classified.

## What changed

Append developer text annotated with `TrustedTool::KIND` to the classification rubric, preserving its authority while keeping user evidence in the input messages. Accept only a single text part with a single matching annotation; continue rejecting other developer messages and unsupported evidence.

## Testing

Add a regression test covering trusted-tool context alongside untrusted user text, plus rejection of incorrect roles, missing or mismatched annotations, multiple annotations or content parts, and image content.

GitOrigin-RevId: 65b6301b2ee1ac54d67275978ccb5e37dcac7c16

Use issuing-step context for Guardian MCP elicitation reviews (#51067)

## Why

MCP elicitation reviews used turn-start context, which could omit remote environments that became ready before the tool invocation and use stale environment permissions.

## What changed

Capture the issuing step's Guardian review context with each live MCP invocation and reuse it for elicitation reviews. Fall back to turn context when no matching live invocation is available, and preserve the captured context for in-flight actions.

## Testing

Extend the deferred-executor regression test to cover MCP elicitations, checking that Guardian receives the newly ready remote environment and its denied paths, excludes stale local denied paths, and returns the denial to the parent model.

GitOrigin-RevId: 0cc58b8f30543a9af87d53e1a90f574a8e6a2f84

Scope Guardian V2 response timing to snapshot sampling (#51065)

## What changed

Measure `responses_duration` directly around `sampler.sample()` in the snapshot classification path. Leave it unset for conversation classification instead of timing submission and waiting for the score.

GitOrigin-RevId: 4cfac9db6f19f3c8513d7bf839ea9631d41bf3ac

Ignore stale refresh responses in agents overview tests (#51064)

## Why

Aborting a refresh task cannot retract a response already queued for delivery. The test helper could consume that stale response and return before the replacement refresh completed.

## What changed

Make `finish_overview_refresh` skip responses whose request ID does not match the active refresh. Extend the lifecycle test to queue an invalidated response before removing a task, exercising the wait for the replacement refresh.

GitOrigin-RevId: 97341681682e8dce9a9512fbcc1d5c0351b084f5

Honor prior cancellation before starting Codex delegates (#51063)

## Why

An already-cancelled delegate spawn can report a runtime admission or startup error instead of `TurnAborted`, including when runtime shutdown has been requested.

## What changed

Check the cancellation token before runtime admission and session startup so prior cancellation returns `TurnAborted` immediately after approval-policy validation.

## Testing

Extend the pre-cancelled spawn test to cover both normal operation and requested runtime shutdown, asserting `TurnAborted` within a one-second timeout.

GitOrigin-RevId: 5a25a211acdd5c246a3c638243ccc8b7240fd051

Gate Guardian continuation tests on classifier request capture (#51061)

## Why

Snapshot classifier requests can arrive out of order, so continuation tests need to keep the next tool blocked until the current tool's classifier request has been captured and checked.

## What changed

Gate every mock Guardian review in high-risk review continuation scenarios. Release each review after checking the corresponding classifier request, preserving the ordering needed by the existing assertions.

GitOrigin-RevId: 9e52acd2bb1ce2fb71100fe0e1b92304d29e9634

Isolate tracing in the strict third-party tool deferral test (#50977)

## Why

The warning assertions need tracing callsite interest to remain independent of untraced parallel tests, even when the test runner already owns the global subscriber.

## What changed

Run the test on a current-thread Tokio runtime and capture warnings with a thread-local subscriber and an explicit buffer. Keep a `NoSubscriber` dispatch alive to stabilize callsite interest, and assert the deferral warning and `client_echo` directly against the captured logs.

GitOrigin-RevId: 5bf22b2cbfefcf8f65016d2cc1444112d9f6a6c7

Track inference tool changes in turn analytics (#50964)

## What changed

Add `tools_change_count` to turn profiles and turn analytics events. Compare the full model-visible tool list before each sampling request, retaining the previous list across turns and connection resets. The first list establishes a baseline; subsequent changes increment the current turn's count.

## Testing

Add coverage for schema changes, tool additions, ordering changes, empty lists, and tracking across sessions and transport fallback. Extend the turn event serialization test to include `tools_change_count`.

GitOrigin-RevId: 44a15c42dc7d0b35c166666faeb9627b718b33dd

Gate stable environment tool exposure behind a feature flag (#50962)

## What changed

Add the default-off `stable_environment_tools` feature flag. When enabled, advertise environment-backed tools before an executor is ready, keep environment selectors stable as readiness changes, and include the `shell` and `login` parameters. Execution still requires a usable environment and its policy.

When disabled, expose environment-backed tools only when a usable environment exists, derive selectors from usable environments, and condition shell parameters on the execution configuration. Restore tool-specific unavailable-environment errors and skip the environment readiness check for `write_stdin`.

## Testing

Parameterize the empty-environment tool availability test for both flag states, check that commands require a ready transport by default, and explicitly opt tests that rely on stable tool exposure into the feature.

GitOrigin-RevId: 68c6240fb3adf85d7f9b407804d4823c515abfdc

Recover malformed Windows deny-read ACL state safely (#50940)

## Why

Malformed `deny_read_acl_state.json` previously caused deny-read ACL reconciliation to fail. Recovery must restore bookkeeping without removing unknown existing restrictions or modifying a linked file's contents.

## What changed

- Retry malformed reads for up to two seconds, then rebuild bookkeeping only after excluding active writers and successfully applying current deny-read ACLs. Preserve unknown historical denies and continue propagating I/O errors.
- Validate the opened state file before reading or writing, rejecting reparse points and files with multiple hard links.
- Write state in place without truncating before validation, preserving file identity and permissions. Retry sharing violations during writes while preventing replacement through delete access.

## Testing

Add Windows tests for corrupt-state recovery, linked-file rejection, concurrent writer and delete-handle behavior, file identity and ACL preservation, and subsequent permission-profile changes. Extend the elevated sandbox integration test to verify that denied reads remain blocked after recovery while allowed writes and deletes succeed.

GitOrigin-RevId: 4aca32df00d015df3763fdc447ffdfbe3fd6cec0

Use server model defaults for connected TUI fresh starts (#50913)

## Why

Fresh starts connected to an app server can bootstrap with stale client model settings before reading the server configuration. An empty model catalog can also prevent startup even when managed new-thread defaults provide a model.

## What changed

- Read server configuration before model bootstrap for fresh starts using a local daemon or remote server without an explicit profile.
- Preserve explicit model and reasoning-effort overrides, clear implicit client settings when `config/read` is unsupported, and allow managed new-thread defaults to supply a model when the catalog is empty.
- Use the launch directory for local daemon configuration reads and the server directory for remote reads.

## Testing

Update startup-default tests to cover managed model selection with an empty catalog. Strengthen the reconnect test with a stale client model and an assertion that `config/read` uses the server directory.

GitOrigin-RevId: 8fe1485c6e66c8d46560b34d904ce1724458993a

Honor server reasoning summary defaults in new TUI threads (#50811)

## Why

New embedded TUI threads forced reasoning summaries off when no summary was explicitly configured, overriding the model's default. Client settings could also override the destination server's reasoning summary configuration.

## What changed

Use the same launch override handling for embedded and remote thread starts so server configuration and model defaults determine reasoning summaries. Forward explicit profile and command-line choices for `model_reasoning_summary` and `features.concurrent_reasoning_summaries`, preserving both enabled and disabled values.

## Testing

Extend coverage for model defaults reaching Responses requests, concurrent summary delivery, direct startup, and replacement sessions with profile and command-line overrides.

GitOrigin-RevId: c60e33d077298d7a89d6b95f94b1292c175d6c77

Prune TUI snapshots and consolidate behavior tests (#50808)

## What changed

- Remove redundant snapshot fixtures and selected rendering test cases across the TUI.
- Replace several full-output snapshots with direct assertions on messages, popup state, status indicators, and rendered content.
- Consolidate slash-command aliases, command-prefix selection, category titles, and hook events into shared test loops.
- Use shared snapshots for the setup import prompt and paginated transcript overlay across platforms.

GitOrigin-RevId: 461e30ebaf70ba930d91a135d2fc598ee4f04f27

Preserve review lifecycle ordering on failure (#50804)

## Why

A review can fail before the UI receives the event that enters review mode. Failed-turn completion also needs to preserve the running indicator when a queued `/review` has already been submitted and is awaiting startup.

## What changed

- Emit the review-entry lifecycle before starting the review task, after aborting existing tasks and clearing connector selection.
- When a live failed-turn completion repeats an already handled error, refresh task state only if no user turn is pending startup, and continue processing queued input.

## Testing

Add regression tests for lifecycle ordering on a server-overload response and for preserving the running indicator while a queued review awaits startup after a failed turn.

GitOrigin-RevId: 0f91d3d1a1a983542c54c2686630de9c232321b1

Use the managed daemon for eligible remote-control launches (#50803)

## What changed

Make plain `codex remote-control` start or reuse the managed daemon and enable remote control when daemon auto-start is enabled and the environment is eligible. Fall back to the foreground server when no managed backend is available or Windows restricts detached launch.

Add `codex remote-control --no-daemon` to explicitly run the foreground server, and honor the top-level `--no-daemon` flag. Reject this flag with `start`, `stop`, or `pair`. Keep `--json` and launches with configuration overrides or unsupported environments on the foreground path.

GitOrigin-RevId: cb28ae3f6074993b748660972c3cb7cbf6612c2f

Fall back to mklink when Windows daemon junction updates are denied (#50802)

## Why

Some Windows policies deny in-process reparse-point mutation while allowing the system junction creator, preventing managed daemon release selection.

## What changed

Fall back to `cmd.exe` with `mklink /J` when native junction creation or retargeting returns `PermissionDenied`. Pass quoted paths through environment variables and disable delayed expansion to handle shell metacharacters.

Create the replacement junction before moving the existing `current` junction aside, and attempt to restore the previous junction if installation fails. Preserve it for recovery if restoration also fails.

## Testing

Extend the Windows junction test to cover fallback creation, native retargeting, and fallback replacement under a path containing spaces, `&`, `%`, and `!`, while verifying that no standalone CLI installation is created.

GitOrigin-RevId: 039ee850f8c788f44f08116614ca3927e3e9952f

Open slash commands from empty drafts in Vim Normal mode (#50788)

## Why

Pressing `/` in Vim Normal mode starts a composer search, even when the draft is empty. Allow this key to open slash commands directly on an empty draft.

## What changed

When slash commands are enabled, a standalone `/` on an empty draft switches to Insert mode, inserts `/`, and opens command completion. Preserve Vim search behavior for nonempty drafts, `?`, and pending operators.

## Testing

Add a snapshot test for the Insert mode transition and command picker. Exercise Vim slash-command entry in the transcript overlay test across terminal sizes, and extend command sparkle coverage to Vim mode.

GitOrigin-RevId: 806c2f6b841190ccdc1a258f88dfa590773ba33a

Remember Command Center grouping across launches (#50786)

## Why

Command Center previously reset to project grouping on startup, losing the user's selected grouping.

## What changed

Save grouping changes to `tui.agents_overview_grouping` in the client’s user configuration and restore the saved choice at startup. Support `project`, `status`, and `model`, with `project` as the default. Report save failures in Command Center while keeping the selected grouping active.

## Testing

Add tests for cycling through and persisting all grouping modes, preserving unrelated settings in a custom configuration file, displaying save errors, and restoring saved grouping during startup.

GitOrigin-RevId: fd56dfecb4b79cfa8439f54420ce58cc0ed66ec7

Retry Windows daemon release publication on transient file locks (#50782)

## Why

Executable scanners can briefly hold newly staged files without delete sharing, causing the rename that publishes a managed daemon release to fail on Windows.

## What changed

Retry publication on permission-denied or sharing-violation errors at 50 ms intervals, up to 100 retries. Report the staging and release paths if publication fails.

## Testing

Add a Windows test that holds the staging directory open without delete sharing, releases the handle after a delay, and verifies that publication succeeds with the payload intact.

GitOrigin-RevId: 4fbd50934ec8937d3b440d38203a2cb7356a316d

Restrict TUI MCP startup notifications to owned threads (#50781)

## Why

MCP startup notifications from unrelated threads could create TUI event channels, allowing subsequent approval requests from those threads to appear in the current session.

## What changed

Check the parent of an untracked subagent before accepting its MCP startup notifications. Read thread metadata with bounded retries for threads that are not yet found or loaded, and ignore notifications unless the parent belongs to the TUI.

Share thread ownership checks across notification and approval routing, including side threads.

## Testing

Extend approval-routing coverage to verify that owned subagent approvals are preserved both before thread-start notifications and after MCP startup notifications, while unrelated threads do not create event channels or display approval prompts.

GitOrigin-RevId: 6f78f237f7441aadf10b491ed191357df75c3a6a

Allow `/archive` while a turn is running (#50764)

## Why

`/archive` was disabled during a running turn, preventing users from archiving the current session until the turn ended.

## What changed

Enable `/archive` during a running turn and warn in the confirmation dialog that archiving will stop the current turn. Cancelling the dialog leaves the turn running.

## Testing

Extend confirmation tests to cover both idle and running sessions, add a snapshot of the running-turn warning, and verify that cancellation leaves the task running without emitting archive events or operations.

GitOrigin-RevId: c7c530aa671b5f04e5dc2a637e3d27a81d98d8bf

Show unavailable slash commands when searched in side conversations (#50756)

## Why

Side conversations hide unavailable slash commands, leaving users without an explanation when searching for a known command.

## What changed

- Show matching unavailable commands as disabled rows with the reason `not available in a side conversation`. For example, `/arch` now shows a disabled `/archive` entry. Keep these commands hidden from the unfiltered `/` menu.
- Rank available matches first and skip disabled rows during keyboard selection and completion.
- Prevent `Tab` from queuing input when only disabled matches are visible, and insert `/` normally when no selectable command is present.

## Testing

Add a rendering snapshot and regression tests for unavailable command discovery, navigation, available command completion and queuing, blocked queuing of unavailable matches, and slash insertion.

GitOrigin-RevId: 7160b308ca57a24a5dcb6e2686b5248a8eb4b6a7

Keep environment-backed tools exposed across readiness changes (#50741)

## Why

Environment readiness previously changed which tools and command parameters were advertised to the model, even when the selected environments stayed the same.

## What changed

- Keep enabled command, patch, image, and permission tools exposed when environments are absent, starting, or failed.
- Return a consistent message asking the model to wait when no usable execution environment is available, while preserving distinct errors for unknown environment IDs.
- Derive environment selectors from all selected environments rather than only ready ones.
- Always advertise `exec_command`'s `shell` and `login` parameters while continuing to enforce login policy at execution time.

## Testing

Expand integration coverage for empty, pending, failed, ready, and recovered environments, including stable command parameters and login-policy rejection. Update subagent and skill-catalog snapshots, with separate Windows expectations.

GitOrigin-RevId: bb08084066896a9f14b3b568c081c3eaac981db7

Show model and reasoning effort near the top of task details (#50727)

## What changed

- Display reasoning effort alongside the model in the agents overview, using `Unknown` when unavailable.
- Place model, reasoning, project, and usage information before attention details, activity, and the last message.
- Truncate long model and reasoning values with an ellipsis to keep each on one line.

## Testing

Update overview snapshots for the new layout and extend fixtures to cover a known model and long model and custom reasoning values.

GitOrigin-RevId: 1f36e5e1e0ccf09a851f8982bbbe4fbc7d9c7461

Decode Windows Terminal's mapped Shift+Enter sequence (#50720)

## Why

Windows Terminal's `sendInput` mapping delivers `ESC[13;2u` as individual console key events. Decode it as `Shift+Enter` so the mapping inserts a newline in the composer.

## What changed

- Wrap the Windows event stream with a decoder for the complete Escape-prefixed sequence, including interleaved key releases.
- Use a fixed 50 ms deadline for partial sequences and replay incomplete or mismatched input unchanged. Preserve literal text, paste events, and native key events.
- Update the `crossterm` revision and dependency lockfiles.

## Testing

Add tests for repeated and fragmented mappings, deadline handling, unchanged input, error and end-of-stream replay, and composer newline rendering with a snapshot.

GitOrigin-RevId: 95ab39960510d71322824c63817710633a2fda23

Let the transport create the Windows remote-control socket directory (#50700)

## Why

Foreground remote control on Windows should let the transport create its socket parent with a protected DACL instead of inheriting the broader ACL from a temporary directory.

## What changed

Use `codex-remote-control/rc-<pid>.sock` under `std::env::temp_dir()` on Windows, leaving parent directory creation to the transport. Keep the existing temporary socket directory behavior on other platforms.

GitOrigin-RevId: 6482ed0fc4ebc6b0e5de4e1d0e13adc93afa56d1

Preserve local Markdown link labels in the TUI (#50695)

## Why

Path-like link labels were collapsed into their destinations, discarding the author's label text and formatting.

## What changed

Preserve nonblank local link labels alongside the formatted destination as `label (target)`, including in tables. Empty or whitespace-only labels show only the destination. Keep destination formatting and fall back to the original destination when a local file URL cannot be parsed.

Render file citations without a label so they continue to display only the formatted destination.

## Testing

Update rendering and transcript-copy tests and snapshots to cover preserved path labels, styled labels, empty labels, malformed file URLs, tables, and Markdown escaping.

GitOrigin-RevId: 2810b70f1ecdc59d7f90fa1b254b1e9069c8fc29

Keep third-party tools deferred in strict Code Mode Only (#50687)

## Why

Third-party exposure settings can eagerly expose tool schemas or exclude tools from `exec`. Keeping eligible tools deferred lets MCP catalogs change between turns without changing the model's eager tool prefix.

## What changed

Add the disabled-by-default `code_mode_only_strict_3p_tools` feature, applied only when the effective model tool mode is Code Mode Only.

- Defer eligible MCP, app, and client-supplied dynamic tools while keeping them discoverable and callable through `exec`.
- Override `deferLoading`, MCP/app `omit_tools_from`, and direct-only or excluded namespace settings. Log conflicts without adding prompt warnings.
- Preserve disabled, app-only, policy-denied, and over-budget tool restrictions. Keep built-in tool exposure unchanged, including when a dynamic tool has the same name.

## Testing

Add unit and integration coverage for exposure overrides, effective model modes, tool eligibility, and app discovery and dispatch. Add an MCP refresh scenario that verifies the eager tool prefix stays unchanged as tools are added, replaced, and removed while `exec` tracks the current catalog.

GitOrigin-RevId: a6a8e401214119bb02ea4711473c8fa3ec85c81a

Allow transcript selection and copying while bottom modals are open (#50564)

## Why

The plan confirmation prompt allowed transcript scrolling but blocked selecting and copying the visible plan text.

## What changed

Allow mouse selection and copying in the visible transcript while a bottom modal is open, preserving drags across redraws. Keep other keyboard input with the modal and suppress transcript link activation, disclosure toggles, and follow-control clicks during modal mouse handling.

## Testing

Extend the plan prompt test to cover selection, `Ctrl+Insert` copying, selection highlighting, and popup bounds. Add coverage confirming that ordinary and Control-clicks do not open links in selection-only mouse handling.

GitOrigin-RevId: 9e1fdfcb4bc18215e62a714f173bc8cb372b090a

Keep Code Mode tool discovery guidance stable across catalog changes (#50562)

## Why

Tool availability can change between calls. Conditioning discovery guidance on whether deferred tools are currently present changes the `exec` description when the catalog changes.

## What changed

Always include the configured discovery guidance in the Code Mode `exec` description, even when no deferred tools are present. The default guidance explains how to find tools in `ALL_TOOLS` and notes that availability can change between calls. Custom guidance and explicit empty overrides remain supported.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for stable guidance with empty and populated deferred tool catalogs in both Code Mode configurations, including custom and empty overrides. Update tool-description assertions and request snapshots.

GitOrigin-RevId: 086ea19a48e3c51ec8c429a619676a936d658721

Distinguish daemon release identity from executable contents (#50559)

## Why

Releases can contain different resources while shipping identical executable bytes. The daemon must recognize those release changes, while a stale updater should be able to hand off without restarting an already-current daemon.

## What changed

- Include a digest of the resolved executable path in `ExecutableIdentity` to distinguish release generations with identical binaries.
- Keep content-only comparisons for package preparation and manual update reporting.
- Check the running daemon's identity and version before restarting during updater adoption, manual updates, and production restoration. Preserve scheduled retries when the daemon is not ready.

## Testing

Add coverage for path-sensitive identity, scheduled no-op updates that preserve the daemon, and resource-only release updates that restart it despite identical executable bytes.

GitOrigin-RevId: bbea06cf502abb2251e70d4ba4b422cae867116c

Avoid reading the current directory when resolving absolute paths (#50558)

## Why

`AbsolutePathBuf::relative_to_current_dir` previously read the current directory even for absolute paths, causing resolution to fail if the current directory had been deleted.

## What changed

Route absolute inputs through `from_absolute_path` without querying the current directory. Relative inputs continue to resolve against the current directory.

## Testing

Extend the Unix regression test to verify that `relative_to_current_dir` succeeds with a deleted current directory and produces the same normalized path as `from_absolute_path`.

GitOrigin-RevId: 6bc6cb43d9f4d57359639708c4d30524d89cfa92

Skip daemon auto-start for Windows-mounted WSL homes (#50555)

## Why

The managed daemon writes an executable and Unix-style state beneath `CODEX_HOME`. Windows-mounted WSL filesystems (DrvFS/9p) do not reliably support the required permission semantics, which can cause startup to fail before the TUI opens.

## What changed

Detect WSL homes on 9p filesystems, checking an existing ancestor when `CODEX_HOME` does not yet exist. Keep the TUI in embedded mode instead of automatically starting the shared background server, and show a startup warning explaining the exclusion.

## Testing

Extend the daemon exclusion warning snapshot to cover the Windows-mounted WSL message.

GitOrigin-RevId: 995e6236d79d8190b0ab1e6b4761eeef3c068467

Keep MCP resource helpers available in code mode (#50546)

## Why

In `CodeModeOnly`, MCP resource helper definitions changed when the first server was added or the last server was removed.

## What changed

Always register `list_mcp_resources`, `list_mcp_resource_templates`, and `read_mcp_resource` in `CodeModeOnly`, even without configured MCP servers. This keeps their definitions stable across server configuration changes.

## Testing

Add a regression scenario that calls all three helpers before adding a server, with a server registered, and after removing it. Assert identical tool definitions across requests, empty resource and template lists, and the expected error when reading from an unknown server.

GitOrigin-RevId: c5777efac250b83dd4bb1c9100a6b6169470556f

Send incremental tool catalog updates in Responses Lite (#50540)

## What changed

When `IncrementalTools` is enabled for Responses Lite, track tool definitions in world state and conversation history. Send the initial catalog once, then append only added or changed definitions while preserving earlier request history. Emit developer notices for removed tools and namespace instruction changes.

Use history-supplied definitions for normal requests and remote compaction, and omit empty `additional_tools` prefixes. Keep the existing tool delivery behavior for the Responses API and when the feature is disabled.

## Testing

Add unit and snapshot coverage for catalog and namespace transitions, empty catalogs, and stable hashing across JSON object key order. Add a request-history scenario covering unchanged tools, a model switch that changes one definition, persisted catalog hashes, and Responses API behavior.

GitOrigin-RevId: 76bde175973b81f8ad23873919da3c8ddcdf6065

Keep shared MCP types stable in Code Mode exec descriptions (#50536)

## Why

Changing a deferred tool's output schema could add or remove the shared MCP type preamble from the `exec` description.

## What changed

Include the default or configured MCP TypeScript preamble whenever `code_mode_only` is enabled, regardless of the available tools' output schemas. Preserve an empty preamble override as a way to omit the section.

## Testing

Add a regression test that checks description stability when a deferred tool gains an MCP output schema, covering default, custom, and empty preambles. Update description expectations, request snapshots, and two Guardian context-budget test thresholds for the added preamble.

GitOrigin-RevId: 725035d6159e9da3c4beff5482c426c082e768b4

Persist realtime transcript tails before closure without inference (#50531)

## Why

When `flush_transcript_tail_on_session_end` is enabled, remaining speech must be available in thread history as soon as realtime closure is reported, even while a model response is still running. Saving that transcript should not trigger another model request.

## What changed

Record the transcript tail directly in model and client history, attaching it to the active turn or creating a completed history turn when idle. Flush persistence before emitting `RealtimeConversationClosed`, and keep realtime context active until recording finishes so the return to text instructions follow the transcript.

## Testing

Extend core and app-server tests to cover immediate history visibility in paginated and legacy modes, idle and active turns, closure without extra inference, transcript reuse in subsequent text turns, and interruption after closure.

GitOrigin-RevId: ae323b711f22aa88db1432e24ad4bb3eb3f08f6b

Reject unknown TUI keys in strict config validation (#50525)

## Why

Flattened notification settings prevent `serde_ignored` from detecting unknown keys in `[tui]`, allowing them to pass `--strict-config` validation.

## What changed

Detect unknown TUI keys by comparing configured keys with a serialized `Tui`, keeping accepted keys derived from the configuration type. Apply this check to config files and `-c`/`--config` overrides so keys such as `tui.bogus_key_xyz` produce an unknown-field error while valid notification settings remain accepted.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for unknown TUI keys, diagnostic source ranges, valid notification settings, and generic validation behavior. Extend CLI tests to cover TUI overrides and config validation before terminal checks.

GitOrigin-RevId: b04467523442183e7a54415d82c3f632f97ef319

Add scenario coverage for remote `/compact` context preservation (#50516)

## What changed

Add a scenario test and snapshot covering the request before remote `/compact`, the compaction request, the persisted replacement history, and the first subsequent user turn.

Capture the replacement history before the next turn can update its context, and assert that the compaction request contains one `compaction_trigger` and the next request includes the returned encrypted checkpoint.

GitOrigin-RevId: e22e12f16bdb11b1296e81a2e0ffd5f70e560ff6

Require GovCloud guidance acknowledgment after Bedrock setup (#50510)

## What changed

After successful Amazon Bedrock setup, check whether the configuration uses AWS GovCloud. If detected, show application configuration and security guidance with a terminal hyperlink and require an explicit Enter press to continue. Allow scrolling in short panes while keeping the acknowledgment visible.

Continue onboarding without the warning for non-GovCloud configurations, failed checks, or checks that exceed the 15-second timeout.

## Testing

Add snapshots and tests for the checking and warning screens, explicit acknowledgment, guidance hyperlinks, and scrolling in short panes, including a one-row content viewport.

Table holdback kept completed tables and subsequent content mutable until the response finished. Releasing completed tables earlier also requires a final scrollback reflow when late reference-link definitions change previously emitted content.

- Release table holdback once the containing top-level Markdown block is stable, rescanning the remaining tail for later tables.
- Track completed-block boundaries across incremental and full renders.
- Request scrollback reflow at answer completion when reference-link definitions are present, including definitions pending without a trailing newline.

## Testing

Add regression assertions and snapshots for completed tables entering scrollback while later tables remain mutable, and for late reference-link definitions resolving correctly at completion. Cover reflow requests with and without a trailing newline and reference handling with inline visualizations enabled.

Advertise `fileWriteStreaming` and support `fs/open` with `mode: "replace"` to create or truncate a file for writing. Implement `fs/writeBlock` with explicit offsets and nonempty chunks of up to 1 MiB, rejecting ranges beyond the signed 64-bit file offset limit.

Upgrade `age` to 0.12.1 and remove the obsolete advisory exception (#50166)

## Why

Local secrets storage pulled in the unmaintained `proc-macro-error2` through `age` and `i18n-embed-fl`, requiring an exception for `RUSTSEC-2026-0173`.

## What changed

GitOrigin-RevId: 7e18dec4d71d9260512f54fbfe71dbe4e6ee8a5d

Bound in-flight file opens in exec-server (#50162)

## Why

The per-connection limit of 128 file read handles was checked only after opening the file, leaving pending opens outside the limit.

## What changed

Reserve a semaphore permit before polling the file-open future, counting pending opens and registered handles against the same limit. Release capacity when an open fails or is cancelled, or when a handle closes, even if a read still retains the file.

Use synchronous handle-table locks that never cross an await, and recheck duplicate IDs after opening to preserve the winning handle during concurrent opens.

## Testing

Add tests for stalled-open progress, pending-open admission limits, permit cleanup after failure or cancellation, capacity reuse while a file remains in use, and concurrent duplicate IDs.

Create worktrees asynchronously and attach them to the requesting task, with ownership and attachments retained across restarts. Default to the repository's remote default branch unless `ref` is supplied. Keep the task's working directory and execution environment unchanged, and leave uncommitted source changes in place.
